blocks.raw: <Tip>Memory aid: **Tactical = temporary, low-cost, quick** (think "guerrilla tactics"—fast, low-resource). **Placemaking = making places meaningful** (the human experience comes first). **Adaptive Reuse = reuse existing buildings** (sustainable, economical). **Gentrification = the risk** (success can displace original communities).</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Treating tactical urbanism as unpermitted vandalism or graffiti. True tactical urbanism is coordinated with municipal authorities; it is not illegal. (Unsanctioned street art may be inspired by tactical urbanism principles but is not itself tactical urbanism.)", "Assuming placemaking and urban regeneration are the same thing. Placemaking is human-sclea activation and community engagement; regeneration is often large-sclea infrastructure redevelopment. They are different but can complement each other.", "Overlooking that adaptive reuse is sustainable. Converting existing buildings (reducing embodied carbon from demolition) is more environmentally friendly than greenfield development or demolition-reconstruction.", "Ignoring gentrification as an inevitable problem rather than a manageable risk. Gentrification can be prevented or mitigated through anti-displacement policies (rent control, community land trusts, affordability preservation, community ownership of development)."]} />
